cards.front: Read to write ratio for a URL shortener, and what it implies
cards.back: About 100 clicks per new link. The redirect path is the system, so optimise it first.

cards.front: 100M new links a month is how many writes per second?
cards.back: About 40 per second, peaking near 120. One database leader could take it.

cards.front: Storage for 6B links at about 500 bytes each
cards.back: About 3 TB, or 9 TB with three replicas: easy for a partitioned key-value store.
302 with a short Cache-Control max-age. A 301 is cached by browsers forever, so you lose analytics and can't take down a phishing link for people who already opened it.

cards.front: How many codes do 7 base62 characters give?
cards.back: 62^7, about 3.5 trillion: nearly 600 times the 6 billion links needed in five years.
7 random base62 characters inserted with a conditional put-if-absent write, retrying on conflict. The database enforces uniqueness and codes can't be enumerated.

cards.front: Why not a global counter for codes?
cards.back: It is a bottleneck and single point of failure, and sequential codes let a scraper walk every link ever made.
Base58 drops the look-alike characters 0, O, I and l, so codes are easier to read and type.

cards.front: The three cache layers on the redirect path
cards.back: CDN edge (max-age about 60 s), then Redis cache-aside with a TTL of a day plus jitter, then the key-value store.

cards.front: Why cache 'not found' for unknown codes?
cards.back: Scrapers guessing random codes would otherwise hammer the database. Caching misses for a minute makes scraping cheap for us.

cards.front: How click analytics stays off the hot path
cards.back: Redirect servers buffer events locally and send batches to Kafka; if Kafka is down old events are dropped rather than slowing redirects.

A conditional write only checks the local region, so two regions can issue the same code within the replication delay. Send all creates to one home region, or give each region its own slice of the code space.

quiz.q: A security team reports a phishing short link. You block it in the database, but users who clicked it yesterday still land on the phishing page. What is the likely cause?
choices: Redirects were served as 301, so browsers cached the destination permanently
Redis TTL is a day plus jitter
quiz.why: A 301 is cached by browsers, so repeat clicks never reach the service and takedowns can't reach them.

quiz.q: A link goes viral in a large newsletter and a million clicks arrive in a minute. Which layer should absorb most of them?
choices: The CDN edge, via Cache-Control max-age=60 on the 302
quiz.why: With a 60 s max-age, a million clicks a minute become about one request per edge location per minute.

quiz.q: A scraper starts guessing random 7-character codes at high volume. What keeps the database safe?
choices: Caching 'not found' results in Redis for about a minute
quiz.why: Unknown codes are cached as not found, so guesses rarely reach the database.

quiz.q: The dashboard compares click totals and finds the service undercounts viral links. What is the most likely gap?
choices: The Redis hit ratio is too high
Clicks answered at the CDN edge never reach the redirect service, so CDN logs must be ingested too
quiz.why: Edge-served clicks only appear in CDN logs, so they need their own pipeline into the same topic.

quiz.q: You run creates in two regions with DynamoDB global tables and random codes. Occasionally a user's link points somewhere else. Why?
choices: Both regions issued the same code within the replication delay and last-writer-wins overwrote one
quiz.why: Conditional writes only check the local copy; use a single write region or partition the code space.

quiz.q: Why does the design recommend random codes over hashing the long URL?
choices: Truncated hashes still collide, and two users can't get separate links and stats for the same URL
Hashes can't be encoded in base62
quiz.why: Hashing needs a collision check anyway and merges different users' links for the same destination.

quiz.q: Kafka becomes unreachable during peak traffic. What should the redirect service do?
choices: Write click events synchronously to the database
Keep redirecting; let the local buffer fill and drop old events
quiz.why: Losing a few clicks is better than slowing redirects.
